stem: Which child is the best candidate for pre- and post-bronchodilator spirometry after a wheezy illness?

options.text: A 2-year-old toddler with viral bronchiolitis history

explanation: An 8-year-old school-aged child is the best candidate for pre- and post-bronchodilator spirometry. Spirometry with bronchodilator reversibility testing is generally suitable for school-aged children rather than infants and preschool children.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because infants are too young for reliable pre- and post-bronchodilator spirometry.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because preschool wheeze is usually not assessed with formal bronchodilator spirometry.
optionExplanations.C: Correct because school-aged children can usually perform reliable spirometry, including pre- and post-bronchodilator testing.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because a 2-year-old is below the age at which spirometry is usually reliable.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because a 4-year-old is still in the preschool age range and is usually too young for reliable spirometry.
